The story, how to help, and who built the data

Berlin Food Map started from a simple frustration. Every time a friend visited, we'd end up sending the same handful of restaurant recommendations over WeChat — losing photos, forgetting addresses, and disagreeing about which place really had the best beef noodles.

We tried a Google Maps list, then a shared spreadsheet, then a Notion doc. None of them captured what mattered: where to actually eat in Berlin if you grew up with Chinese food.

So we started this project. It's open-source, non-profit, and built around a simple idea — the people who eat at a place should be the ones describing it. The restaurant data lives as plain YAML files in a public GitHub repository, easy for anyone to read, fork, or improve. The app is free, ad-free, and stores nothing about you.

It's a love letter, really — to the small noodle shops, the family-run Sichuan kitchens, the late-night dumpling spots that don't show up in Google's top picks. If we've helped you find your next favourite, that's the whole point.
Pulled live from the project's git history — every commit that touches the restaurant data files. If you've contributed and we missed you, open an issue and we'll fix it.
No contributors yet — be the first!

Berlin Food Map is a non-profit project, kept alive by the people who eat here. New places open every month, old favourites move or close, and no single team can keep up alone. If you've spotted a noodle shop we're missing, an address that has gone stale, or a phone number nobody picks up — we'd love a hand.
• A restaurant we don't have yet — the name, address, and anything you remember.
• Corrections — closed places, renamed shops, wrong opening hours, bad coordinates.
• Cuisine and dish tags — Sichuan, Cantonese, Northeastern home-style; whatever helps the next person find their match.
• Photos, a personal note, or a one-line recommendation we can quote.
1. The easy way — send a CSV, Excel, or Google Sheet to our team. One row per restaurant, columns however you like; we'll clean it up on our side.
2. The hands-on way — open a pull request on GitHub. Restaurant data lives as YAML files in data/restaurants. Edit one, propose a change, and the CI pipeline syncs it live.
3. The casual way — drop a message in the WeChat community group or tag us on Xiaohongshu. We'll add the tip to the review queue.

Every submission is reviewed by a real person, cross-checked with Google Places for hours and coordinates, and goes live on the next data sync — usually within a few days. Contributions are anonymous by default; if you'd like a credit on the contributors list, just say so.

Novawerk is an open, non-profit community hub. We exist to lower the barriers to creating positive change — helping people turn meaningful ideas into real projects through collaboration, creativity, and action.

Great ideas shouldn't stay as concepts. Real change happens when people choose to build, learn, and contribute together, instead of waiting for someone else to do it.

Three ideas guide what we do: innovation should create real positive change, not chase short-term trends; people of any background can grow through practical work on real projects together; and everyone shares the responsibility to care, contribute, and act.

Berlin Food Map is one of the projects built under that idea.

Pinwo is a Berlin-based Chinese dining brand. They curate restaurants across the city, run a partner program with member deals and tasting events, and help newcomers and long-timers alike find places worth coming back to.\n\nPinwo is our co-brand partner on Berlin Food Map — same city, same scene, complementary takes on it: they curate the dining experience for their members; Berlin Food Map maps every Chinese restaurant in Berlin we can find, free and open to anyone.

Berlin Chinese Food Map — including the app code and the restaurant data — is open-source on GitHub. The full licence text is public; this screen lists the essentials and the attributions for the third-party libraries we depend on.

Everything in this repository — the Kotlin Multiplatform app, the web apps, the pipeline scripts, and the restaurant data — is licensed under the MIT License. You may use, copy, modify, and redistribute the project freely, including for commercial use, as long as you keep the original copyright notice and this permission notice with any substantial portions you reuse.

This app is built on open-source libraries — Compose Multiplatform, Material 3, AndroidX, Coil, Ktor, kotlinx-datetime, kotlin-inject, gitlive Firebase KMP, kmp-maps-compose, Compass, and the Firebase + Google Maps SDKs. Each is distributed under its own licence (Apache-2.0 or MIT). The full list, with attributions, lives in the GitHub repository.
